passage: Hiroshi, two, was pushing the lid of his pop-up toy when the clown sprang out. His eyes went wide, he gasped, and he jerked back onto Noa's lap. Noa laughed lightly and said, "Surprise!" Hiroshi watched her face, then giggled and pushed the lid down again. He waited, tense, and when the clown popped out, squealed with delight. Noa kept her voice easy each time.

qa.q: What toy surprised Hiroshi?
qa.a: A pop-up toy with a clown surprised him.

qa.q: What does Hiroshi's watching Noa's face suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests he checks her reaction to decide if the surprise is safe. He might also have been waiting to see the clown again.

qa.q: What did Noa do that helped turn surprise into laughter?
qa.a: She stayed relaxed, laughed lightly and named it, so Hiroshi could feel safe. 😊

qa.q: What might change if Noa had looked alarmed?
qa.a: Hiroshi might read fear from her and cry instead of laughing.

grounding: A toddler widens the eyes, gasps and startles at a pop-up toy, and surprise can turn to laughter depending on trust and calm.

passage: I am Chaitanya, and on the train platform a balloon popped near a toddler, Lalit, who was holding his father's hand. Lalit's eyes went wide, he gasped and stiffened. His father knelt and said, "That was a big pop! It's okay." Lalit stared, then his face wobbled, and he hid it against his father's leg. A moment later he peeked out and let out a small giggle. I could not tell which feeling won.

qa.q: What did Lalit's father say after the pop?
qa.a: He said, "That was a big pop! It's okay."

qa.q: What does Lalit's wobbling face and hiding suggest, and what else might the giggle mean?
qa.a: It suggests he was frightened at first and then felt safe again. The giggle might be relief, or amusement at the game of hiding.

qa.q: What did Lalit's father do that helped?
qa.a: He stayed calm and close and named what happened in a few simple words.

qa.q: How does Chaitanya describe what he saw?
qa.a: Chaitanya says openly that they could not tell which feeling won, since they can see only Lalit's face and body.

grounding: A toddler gasps and startles at a sudden sound, and surprise can turn to fear or laughter depending on trust and calm reaction.

passage:
Monday: at a party, a popper went bang. Afreen startled and looked at Zubin, her father. He had jumped too, face worried. Afreen burst into tears.
Wednesday: a balloon popped at home. Zubin laughed calmly. "Pop!" Afreen startled, looked at him, then laughed.
The next Monday: Afreen squeezed a bubble and it popped. She gasped, eyes wide, looked at Zubin, and giggled.

qa.q: What popped on Wednesday?
qa.a: A balloon.

qa.q: Why did Afreen cry on Monday but laugh on Wednesday?
qa.a: On Monday she saw her father's worried face and felt frightened; on Wednesday his calm laugh made the surprise feel safe and funny.

qa.q: What did Zubin learn over the week?
qa.a: That his calm reaction helps Afreen turn a surprise into laughter instead of fear.

qa.q: How might Zubin feel the next Monday?
qa.a: He would likely feel pleased and relieved that Afreen now finds surprises fun.

grounding: Over a week a father learns his calm reaction turns his toddler's surprise into laughter rather than fear.

passage:
Dolma from next door handed Bhupen a round tin in their Guwahati flat. "Open it."
He pulled the lid, and a cloth snake sprang out. Bhupen gasped, eyes huge, and dropped the tin. He froze, looking at Dolma's face.
Dolma smiled wide. "Surprise! A silly snake!" Bhupen let out a shaky laugh, then a real one, and pushed the snake back in to try again.

qa.q: What sprang out of the tin?
qa.a: A cloth snake.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling when he froze and looked at Dolma?
qa.a: He was surprised and unsure whether to be scared; her smile made him feel safe, so he laughed.

qa.q: What did Dolma do that helped Bhupen?
qa.a: She smiled and named it a silly surprise, showing it was safe.

qa.q: What would change if Dolma had shrieked too?
qa.a: Bhupen would likely have read it as danger and cried instead of laughing.

grounding: A toddler gasps at a pop-up toy and checks a neighbour's face, whose calm smile turns surprise into laughter.

passage:
"Cuckoo! Cuckoo!" The little bird shot out of the clock.
Ishita gasped and froze, eyes wide, spoon halfway to her mouth.
"Is she scared?" asked her mother.
"Cuckoo says hello, Ishita!" said Neelam, her Nani, calmly waving at it.
Ishita looked at Nani, then at the clock. The bird popped back in. She laughed and pointed.
"Again?"
"Next hour," said Nani, smiling.

qa.q: What shot out of the clock?
qa.a: A little bird.

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling when she froze?
qa.a: She was surprised and unsure, checking Nani's face to see if it was safe; Nani's calm made her laugh.

qa.q: What did Neelam do that helped?
qa.a: She stayed calm and made the bird friendly by saying it was saying hello and waving.

qa.q: How does Ishita's mother first read the gasp?
qa.a: She wonders if Ishita is scared.

grounding: A toddler freezes in surprise at a cuckoo clock, and her grandmother's calm reaction turns it into laughter.

passage:
Note from Pranav at the creche, for Sunaina's parents

Today a balloon burst near the window. Sunaina's eyes went wide, she gasped and went stiff all over. Her lip started to wobble and she looked straight at me. I smiled, kept my voice slow and said, "Pop! Big noise." Then I clapped once, softly. She stared at me, then giggled and clapped too. All afternoon she kept whispering "pop!" to her doll. 😊

qa.q: What burst near the window?
qa.a: A balloon burst near the window.

qa.q: What does Sunaina's wobbling lip and her look at Pranav suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She was most likely startled and a little frightened by the sudden bang, and looked at Pranav to check whether she was safe. Her giggle a moment later shows the surprise could also tip into amusement.

qa.q: Which choice worked here, and why?
qa.a: Pranav stayed calm, smiled and named the noise in a slow voice, so Sunaina read that she was safe and her surprise turned into laughter.

qa.q: What would change if Pranav had jumped and shouted too?
qa.a: Sunaina would probably have picked up Pranav's alarm, and her surprise might have turned into crying and fear instead of a game.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler's wide-eyed, gasping surprise at a sudden sound turning to laughter because the caregiver stays calm.
